title: Implement burst pool admission controller service (APIs, state, integration tests)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Build the Burst Admission Controller service (BAC) responsible for deciding whether a Dedicated tenant request may exceed reserved baseline by borrowing GPUs from a region/hardware-class burst pool.

This ticket covers:
- Service implementation + deployable artifact
- Public-ish (gateway/routing-facing) admit API(s)
- State model required for fairness/cooldowns + idempotency
- Integration tests (multi-tenant scenarios, telemetry lag scenarios)

Non-goals (in this ticket):
- Console UI (tracked separately)
- Full billing export pipeline (separate ticket)
- Cross-region bursting (out of scope for initial release)

References:
- Confluence design spec: sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/burst-admission-controller-service.json
- ADR (admission semantics): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-burst-pool-admission-control-semantics.json
- ADR (fairness model): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-fairness-model-for-shared-burst-pools.json
- Related routing integration: ENG-4812
- Tenant config schema: ENG-4816

Owner notes:
We must be conservative by default: if telemetry is stale or dependencies are unhealthy, deny burst (serve baseline only) and return explicit denial reason codes so support and customers can understand behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Admission API is implemented and stable for routing to call in the hot path.
2) Decisions are deterministic given an idempotency key and a stable policy/config snapshot.
3) Fairness + guardrails state is implemented: per-tenant caps, cooldown windows, pool safety limits.
4) Service fails closed for burst (deny burst) when telemetry is stale/unavailable.
5) Integration tests cover:
   - multi-tenant fairness under contention
   - cooldown enforcement
   - telemetry lag/staleness handling
   - circuit breaker interactions (global safety cap)
6) Metrics and logs exist to explain admit/deny at aggregate and per-tenant level (high level only; detailed dashboards tracked elsewhere).
7) Rollout gating hooks exist (feature flag + per-tenant allowlist + per-region/hardware allowlist).
technical_plan:
API surface (routing-facing)
- Endpoint: POST /v1/burst/admit
  - Purpose: determine if a given request is allowed to consume burst capacity right now.
  - Request fields (conceptual; final schema lives in proto/openapi):
    - tenant_id
    - request_id (or idempotency_key)
    - region
    - hardware_class (e.g., H100, L40S)
    - baseline_allocation (reserved GPUs / capacity units)
    - requested_increment (additional GPUs/capacity units over baseline)
    - model_id (for observability only; not used to admit initially)
    - priority_tier (e.g., default/silver/gold)
    - now_ms (optional; for test harness only)
  - Response fields:
    - admitted: true|false
    - decision_id (for tracing)
    - reason_code (standardized denial/admit code)
    - retry_after_ms (set for backoff guidance)
    - effective_limit_snapshot (optional, redacted, internal-only)

- Endpoint: GET /internal/burst/decision/{decision_id}
  - Purpose: internal debugging/support tooling (redacted) to explain decision inputs and the guardrail that triggered.
  - Must be protected by RBAC; do not leak pool-level sensitive numbers to customer-facing surfaces.

Core decision flow
1) Read tenant burst config (from control plane cache) + policy rules (policy engine) for:
   - burst_enabled
   - max_burst_ratio
   - per-tenant max increment
   - cooldown window
   - priority tier weights
2) Read pool telemetry snapshot (from fleet telemetry aggregator):
   - pool_capacity_total
   - pool_capacity_available
   - pool_saturation
   - telemetry_age_ms
3) Hard safety gates (fail-closed):
   - if !burst_enabled => deny (TENANT_BURST_DISABLED)
   - if request exceeds tenant cap => deny (TENANT_CAP_EXCEEDED)
   - if telemetry_age_ms > staleness_threshold => deny (TELEMETRY_STALE)
   - if global circuit breaker open => deny (FLEET_SAFETY_CIRCUIT_OPEN)
   - if pool safety headroom breached => deny (POOL_SAFETY_LIMIT)
4) Fairness gate:
   - Apply per-tenant token bucket / weighted allocation (per ADR) to avoid starvation and prevent a single tenant from consuming entire pool.
   - Maintain per-tenant spend over a rolling window.
   - If insufficient tokens => deny (FAIRNESS_RATE_LIMIT)
5) Cooldown gate:
   - If tenant recently burst above threshold and cooldown not elapsed => deny (COOLDOWN_ACTIVE)
6) Admit:
   - Reserve burst increment for a short TTL (soft reservation) to reduce race conditions.
   - Emit decision metrics + structured log.

State & storage
- Required state:
  - per-tenant fairness bucket counters (by region+hw_class)
  - per-tenant cooldown last_burst_ts
  - short-lived reservations keyed by idempotency_key
- Storage approach:
  - Use Redis (or existing platform KV) for shared state across replicas.
  - Keep small in-memory cache for hot reads with short TTL; all writes go to shared store.
- Idempotency:
  - Same (tenant_id, idempotency_key) must return the same decision within decision_ttl.
  - Prevent double-counting of fairness spend on retries.

Determinism requirements
- Deterministic within a time slice: the same input tuple + same config snapshot + same idempotency key must yield identical admit/deny and reason_code.
- Telemetry smoothing: apply an EWMA / monotonic staleness guard so the controller does not oscillate admit/deny when telemetry is delayed.

Observability (minimum for this ticket)
- Metrics:
  - bac_admit_requests_total{region,hw_class,result,reason_code,priority_tier}
  - bac_pool_telemetry_age_ms{region,hw_class}
  - bac_state_store_errors_total
  - bac_reservation_conflicts_total
  - bac_latency_ms{endpoint}
- Logs:
  - Structured decision log with: tenant_id hash, decision_id, reason_code, policy_version, telemetry_age_ms.

Deployment & rollout
- Service deployed in platform cluster per region.
- Feature flag gates:
  - global enable
  - per region/hw allowlist
  - per tenant allowlist
- Safe fallback:
  - If BAC unavailable, routing should treat as deny burst and continue at baseline.

Testing
- Unit tests:
  - fairness bucket math + edge cases
  - cooldown enforcement
  - idempotency behavior
- Integration tests:
  - simulated multi-tenant contention with fixed telemetry snapshots
  - induced telemetry lag and validation of fail-closed behavior
  - reservation TTL expiry + retry behavior
  - circuit breaker open/close transitions
- Contract tests:
  - schema validation for request/response + reason codes list stability
denial_reason_codes:
Initial reason code set (must match gateway/routing expectations):
- TENANT_BURST_DISABLED
- TENANT_CAP_EXCEEDED
- TENANT_NOT_ALLOWLISTED
- REGION_HW_NOT_ENABLED
- TELEMETRY_STALE
- POOL_SATURATED
- POOL_SAFETY_LIMIT
- FAIRNESS_RATE_LIMIT
- COOLDOWN_ACTIVE
- FLEET_SAFETY_CIRCUIT_OPEN
- INTERNAL_ERROR (only when we can confidently say it is controller-local; prefer TELEMETRY_STALE / dependency-specific codes where possible)

Notes:
- Denials should include retry_after_ms when backoff is appropriate.
- Some denials should be treated as "do not retry" (e.g., TENANT_BURST_DISABLED, TENANT_NOT_ALLOWLISTED).
rollout_notes:
Dogfood plan:
- Start with internal Dedicated workloads in us-east / H100 burst pool only.
- Gate on: no statistically significant p95/p99 regression for non-burst tenants, and denial reason distribution matches expected (mostly FAIRNESS_RATE_LIMIT / POOL_SAFETY_LIMIT under load).

Rollback plan:
- Flip global burst enable flag off (BAC still running but always returns deny burst).
- If needed: disable by region/hw allowlist.
- If BAC is causing latency in routing path: routing fallback to baseline-only without BAC call (separate routing kill switch).

risks_and_mitigations:
Key risks
- Telemetry lag causes unfair denials or admit oscillations.
  Mitigation: staleness thresholds + EWMA smoothing + deterministic idempotency decisions.
- State store latency impacts routing hot path.
  Mitigation: strict timeouts, fast deny path, caching, and ensure routing can bypass BAC in emergency.
- Label cardinality in metrics/logs becomes unbounded.
  Mitigation: never label by tenant_id; use tier and reason_code only.
- Incorrect idempotency semantics leads to double-spend / inconsistent decisions.
  Mitigation: reservation keyed by idempotency_key; integration tests for retry paths.

Operational notes
- BAC must fail closed for burst. Worst case: customer can’t burst (but baseline remains intact), which is preferable to fleet SLO regression.
